t: That, in order to provide for more effective accomplishment of the purposes of the Act entitled “An Act to promote conservation in the arid and semiarid areas of the United States by aiding in the development of facilities for water storage and utilization”, approved August 28, 1937, as amended (50 Stat. 869; 16 U. S. C. 590r–x; 54 Stat. 1124, 16 U. S. C. 590z–5), section 7 of the Act relating to water conservation and utilization projects in the Great Plains and the arid and semiarid areas of the United States approved October 14, 1940 (54 Stat. 1124: 16 U. S. C. 590z–5), is hereby amended by striking the figures “$50,000” and inserting in lieu thereof the figures “$100,000”.

fable.w: This section only raises a dollar limit in an existing water conservation statute from $50,000 to $100,000. The tempting reading is that a statute about water conservation projects in the Great Plains must involve states or local interests, but nothing in the text provides for consultation, hearings, rulemaking, an advisory body, or a right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: is hereby amended by striking the figures “$50,000” and inserting in lieu thereof the figures “$100,000”

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple appropriation amendment that increases a funding cap from $50,000 to $100,000. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely a legislative adjustment of financial limits.
qwen_block.s: section 7 of the Act relating to water conservation and utilization projects in the Great Plains and the arid and semiarid areas of the United States approved October 14, 1940 (54 Stat. 1124: 16 U. S. C. 590z–5), is hereby amended by striking the figures “$50,000” and inserting in lieu thereof the figures “$100,000”.

opus.w: The section only amends an existing statute by raising a dollar figure from $50,000 to $100,000. No one outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision: there is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. References to water conservation projects are background only and do not create any participation process.
opus.s: is hereby amended by striking the figures “$50,000” and inserting in lieu thereof the figures “$100,000”
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The section mentions "conservation," "water storage and utilization," and federal "projects," which might suggest that states or local water users are involved. That fails the definition. The amendment only changes a dollar figure in an earlier statute. It names no outside party and sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue.
